1.why: All six screenshots show a static page layout with no moving images, animations, or pop-ups.

2.why: Blue primary buttons, bold headings, and highlighted info boxes make the main actions and key notices visually prominent on every step.

3.why: Each screen has a clear step label (Step X of 5), descriptive heading, single labeled input, and obvious primary button so the needed action is immediately findable.

4.why: The user must follow five sequential steps and retain password-composition rules plus one-time tokens copied from the log panel, so many rules and steps must be remembered.

5.why: No password-manager, autofill, or “remember me” controls or prompts appear on any of the password or token entry screens.

6.why: All input fields are empty and no previously saved or familiar account items are displayed for recognition.

7.why: Instructional text and labels across the screens are brief, plainly worded, and easy to read.

8.why: No error messages are shown in any screenshot, so the system does not demonstrate messages that describe problems or fixes.

9.why: Password rules are listed but no concrete example values (e.g., sample passwords or token formats) are provided in the fields or tips.

10.why: The flow offers only a single fixed path (password reset + MFA code) with no visible choices among password, code, face, or other login methods.

11.why: Each step presents essentially one input and one primary action, so the user is not given many choices at once.

12.why: Step titles, progress labels, informational banners, and the final “Privacy statement accepted” screen clearly state the result of each action.

13.why: Every step includes short tip boxes (blue info panels and the persistent “Stay safe” anti-phishing reminder) that guide the user.

14.why: A “Return to recovery request” link exists on step 2, but other screens show no explicit retry or back controls for correcting mistakes.

15.why: All six screens share the identical header, two-column card layout, typography, and “Stay safe” panel, keeping the design consistent.
